sections.summary: Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the Lord's disciples, obtains letters from the high priest to the synagogues at Damascus to bring any who belong to the Way, both men and women, bound to Jerusalem.

sections.section_title: The Encounter on the Road to Damascus
sections.summary: A light from heaven flashes around Saul; he falls to the ground and hears the voice of Jesus asking 'Why are you persecuting Me?'; Saul is blinded for three days, during which he neither eats nor drinks.

sections.section_title: The Vision to Ananias and the Commission of Saul
sections.summary: The Lord appears to Ananias in a vision and sends him to Saul, calling Saul a 'chosen instrument' (skeuos ekloges) to bear God's name before Gentiles, kings, and the sons of Israel, and declaring that Saul will be shown how much he must suffer for Jesus's name. The 'chosen instrument' language describes vocational calling -- election to a specific mission and purpose -- not a guarantee of individual eternal salvation.

Ananias goes to Saul, lays hands on him, addresses him as 'Brother Saul,' declares that the Lord Jesus who appeared to him on the road has sent him so that Saul may regain his sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit; something like scales falls from Saul's eyes and he is baptized.

Saul spends several days with the disciples in Damascus and immediately begins proclaiming Jesus in the synagogues, declaring that Jesus is the Son of God; all who hear are amazed; Saul keeps increasing in strength and confounding the Jews by proving that Jesus is the Christ.

sections.section_title: The Plot Against Saul and His Escape
sections.summary: After many days the Jews plot together to kill Saul; their plot becomes known; the disciples lower him in a basket through an opening in the city wall by night.

Saul comes to Jerusalem and tries to associate with the disciples, but they are all afraid of him; Barnabas brings him to the apostles and describes his conversion and bold preaching; Saul speaks boldly in Jesus's name, disputes with the Hellenistic Jews, and when the brethren learn of a plot against his life, they send him to Tarsus.
The church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria enjoys peace, is built up, and continues to increase, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

Peter travels to Lydda, finds a paralyzed man named Aeneas who has been bedridden for eight years, heals him in the name of Jesus Christ, and all who live at Lydda and Sharon see him and turn to the Lord.

In Joppa, a disciple named Tabitha (Dorcas) who was full of good works and charity falls sick and dies; Peter is summoned, prays, and raises her from the dead; the miracle becomes known throughout Joppa and many believe in the Lord.
